title: رحلة ابن بطوطة (Riḥlat Ibn Baṭṭūṭa)
shelf_note: An Arabic printed edition of Ibn Battuta's Riḥla, on the Arabic-language shelf. The page is the Delhi section, on Muhammad bin Tughluq's executions.
structure_note: The printed page number is (٧٠) at record 378, so the pagination restarts partway through the book. This fits a multi-volume edition bound or scanned together, and it would explain most of the 232 printed_repeats. The 13 backsteps are probably misread numerals or the volume restart, not a splice. The structure count pages_translated = 0 contradicts pages_translated_field = 568 and this page's stored translation, so the count is unreliable (E2).

pages.layout: single column of prose under a centred page number and a rule; two centred section headings set between ornamental brackets

ocr_errors.problem: The alif of خالف ('rebelled') is dropped, giving خاف ('feared'). The translation's note then blames this OCR slip on the printer.

ocr_errors.image: فقال هلا قلت هذا قبل موته
ocr_errors.problem: هلا is dropped, so the Sultan's rebuke ('why did you not say this…') becomes a statement ('you said this…'). The translation follows the image.
يعفى ('pardoned') is misread as يغني. The translation has the right sense.
فوشي ('informed on') is garbled to في
جعل is misread as جيل, and the possessive is lost
an extra letter in the name Bakht

tr_errors.english: <note>The printed text reads "khāfa" (feared), most likely an error for "khālafa" (rebelled).</note>
tr_errors.problem: The note claims a misprint that does not exist. The image prints خالف, so the 'error' is the OCR's. The rendering 'rebelled' is right, but the note gives the source a corruption it does not have.

other.note: An invented textual note: the translation tells the reader the printed text has a misprint ("khāfa" for "khālafa") that is not on the leaf.
Centring arrows leak into the English headings: "-> ❖ Account of his execution of Tughan and his brother ❖ <-" and "-> ❖ Account of his execution of the son of the Malik al-Tujjar ❖ <-".

missing.english: word reached the Sultan that Sheikh al-Haydari had prayed for Judge Jalal
missing.why: The page never names 'the Sultan'. A general reader needs to be told this is Muhammad bin Tughluq, Sultan of Delhi, whose executions the section lists.

missing.english: When the rebellion of Ain al-Mulk broke out, with his rising and his fighting against the Sultan, as we shall relate
missing.why: Ain al-Mulk and his revolt are referred to as if already known. A short note (a governor who rose against the Sultan, told later in the book) would orient the reader.

book_verdict: The transcription has several letter-level misreadings, two of which change the meaning. The English follows the image closely and is faithful. But one note invents a printer's error to explain away an OCR slip, and an expert reader would notice that false apparatus, so the page counts as having a defect on sight.
